text:
customer_alex: Hey team — running into intermittent 401s calling /v1/respond from our webapp. Happens in Chrome + Safari. Console shows "401 Unauthorized" and a request id: req_ABC123. Happening ~every 10-20 requests.
maya (Support): thanks for the report, alex. can you grab a HAR + console logs from Chrome and Safari and upload? we need the network payload + request headers and the request id.
customer_alex: yep can do. quick Q — do you want the full logs or redact the auth token?
oliver (SRE): include full headers as-is in the HAR (do NOT paste token into slack). you can redact the token before posting here by replacing with <REDACTED>. i mainly need x-request-id and response headers/body. also note the approximate local time of the failure.
maya (Support): steps below — follow the browser you hit it in. keep the exact request attempt that produced req_ABC123.
maya (Support): Chrome/Edge/Brave: 1) Open DevTools (F12) -> Network tab. 2) Check "Preserve log". 3) Check "Disable cache" (optional). 4) Reproduce the issue so the error appears. 5) Right click on any request -> "Save all as HAR with content". 6) Console tab -> right click -> "Save as..." to capture console logs if you want separate file. 7) Attach both files to the upload link below.
maya (Support): Safari (mac): 1) Enable Develop menu (Safari -> Preferences -> Advanced -> Show Develop menu). 2) Develop -> Show Web Inspector -> Network. 3) Preserve log (top-left). 4) Reproduce. 5) Right-click a request -> Export -> "Export HAR" or use "File -> Export-> Export HAR" on newer versions. 6) Console -> Save the console output.
maya (Support): Firefox: Network tab -> gear -> "Enable persistent logs" -> reproduce -> Right click -> "Save all as HAR".
maya (Support): chrome://net-export (Chrome) is helpful for very noisy network cases — start logging, reproduce, stop, then attach the .json net-export file. only do this if HAR misses the issue.
maya (Support): sample curl you can run locally to reproduce a single request (swap token and body):
```
curl 'https://api.redwood.inference/v1/respond' 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' 
  -H 'x-request-id: req_ABC123' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  --data-raw '{"input":"hello"}' 
  --compressed -v
```
oliver (SRE): if you want to capture the outgoing browser request headers for us to compare, you can copy the request as curl from the network tab (right click -> Copy -> Copy as cURL) and paste here after redacting the token. that helps validate signing/time skew issues.
maya (Support): when you upload, include: 1) the HAR (with content), 2) console log, 3) timestamp of repro, 4) approximate user id / account id, 5) the request id(s) you saw (e.g., req_ABC123).
customer_alex: cool — uploading now. link?
har-uploader-bot: Hi @customer_alex — please use this pre-signed upload link to attach logs: https://uploads.redwood.ai/support/abcdef (expires in 24h). Reply here when uploaded.
customer_alex: uploaded: 
- alex_chrome_req_ABC123.har (19MB)
- alex_console_2026-03-16.log
maya (Support): got the files, thanks. forwarding to SRE for correlation. oliver, assigning to you — time window ~ 15:23:40 PST, request id req_ABC123.
oliver (SRE): confirmed receipt. i'll pull logs for req_ABC123 and check auth service trace + token validation. if we need deeper instrumentation i'll request a net-export from the user or a debug-bundle (we can generate a small client-side trace helper).
maya (Support): one more note — if the customer can reproduce in an incognito window and still see the 401, that rules out extension interference. please try that too.
customer_alex: will try incognito and report back in ~10m. thanks :thumbsup:
